task.name: Applying an accepted decomposition proposal is a separate mutation from producing it
task.story_text:
---
depends_on:
  - issue-2686
---

## What

An operator who accepts a decomposition proposal has forge apply it: create one issue per
proposed slice, write the dependency edges where the scheduler reads them, close the original
as decomposed, and record the disposition. Producing the proposal is separate work; this is
the mutation that acts on it.

## Why

Producing a proposal and applying one carry different risks. A proposal is an artifact the
operator reads and can ignore at no cost. Applying it mutates the issue tracker — new issues,
declared edges, the original closed — and a bad proposal that was applied costs more to undo
than one that was declined. Separating them lets the proposal ship first and be measured
against whether accepted splits actually land, before anything acts on it automatically.

The separation also keeps each piece within single-story scope. Carried together, the
deliberation, the proposal schema, dependency inference, issue creation, edge writing and
audit disposition are the shape the complexity pause exists to catch.

## Acceptance criteria

- Accepting a proposal creates one issue per proposed slice, each carrying that slice's title
  and scope boundary.
- Every dependency edge the proposal declares is written into the created issue bodies at
  creation time, in the form the sprint scheduler reads, rather than added afterwards.
- The original story is closed as decomposed, distinguishable from one closed as completed.
- Nothing is created without an explicit operator acceptance. A proposal that is declined, or
  left unanswered until the pause resolves by any other route, creates nothing and leaves the
  original story intact and runnable.
- A failure partway through leaves a state the operator can act on rather than a half-applied
  split: what was created is reported, and the original story is not closed unless every slice
  was created and every declared edge written.
- The audit records the proposal as applied and its disposition, so a later measurement can ask
  whether accepted splits landed.

## Example

```
PAUSE     → #2541 scored 10, scope exceeded. Proposal (4 slices) attached.
OPERATOR  → forge decide 7c1e04b9d3af accept

APPLIED   → created #2900  extract the portable diagnosis record
            created #2901  route diagnosis through the record      depends_on #2900
            created #2902  port the CLI surface                    depends_on #2900
            created #2903  cross-project acceptance                depends_on #2901, #2902
            closed  #2541  decomposed
            audit   proposal applied, disposition accepted
```

Declining instead creates nothing and leaves #2541 exactly as it was.

correspondences.description: proposal_is_appliable decides whether accept is offered using only the task's cached type field, while _read_context later refuses the application unless the live tracker issue carries exactly one appliable type label, so an issue whose labels were edited after intake (or that carries two type labels) is offered an accept that can only fail after the operator has committed to it.

In _validated_slices, a non-integer depends_on entry refuses the whole application while a non-integer covers_criteria entry is silently dropped, so a proposal with corrupted criteria mapping applies with the scope-boundary fallback substituted for the criteria the operator read in the proposal.

An expired pending record carrying accept and a restored accept whose recorded source is no_decision both create the slices and close the original even though neither is a valid active operator acceptance.
When application is interrupted after its first slice is created, re-entry creates that same slice again and leaves the earlier issue absent from the recorded partial state.

When the pending poller returns accept while the pending record's decided_at is later than its timeout_at, the gate records an operator accept and creates the slice issues and closes the source issue.

When a recorded accept is refused by the provenance guard on a state that already carries created slices from an earlier partial application, _refuse_application records the outcome with an empty created tuple and _record_application overwrites the persisted slice list with that empty list, discarding the run record's only handle on the issues that already exist.

When application stops after the first issue-create call returns but before its callback records the slice, the durable state contains accept with no application status, so re-entry disables marker reconciliation and creates the first slice again.

When an enhancement is relabeled as a bug after intake, application treats the missing appliable label as a removal, creates enhancement slices from the stale intake type, and closes the live bug issue.

handoff.summary: Added a deterministic, coordinator-side path that applies an accepted decomposition proposal. New module `coordinator/decomposition_application.py` validates the recorded assessment, orders slices so every dependency is created first, renders each slice body (leading `depends_on:` frontmatter naming the upstream issues, the prose half of each edge, the slice scope, the original acceptance criteria it covers, a stable `forge-decomposition-v1` marker), validates each body through the shared issue-shape gate as RUNNABLE before creating anything, creates via `gh issue create` carrying the original's type label and milestone, and closes the original last with `--reason "not planned"` through `spike_guard.check_spike_closure`. The gate gained `accept`/`decline` in a vocabulary deliberately split from the fallback-eligible one (`PREFLIGHT_GATE_ACTIONS` still governs `normalize_preflight_gate_no_decision`), offered only when an assessment was generated, the story is GitHub-issue-backed, and its type is one a slice can satisfy. Accept returns a terminal applied result that `returned_for_decomposition` (now shared by audit, sprint runner and `cli/run`) reports as decomposed; a partial application returns a terminal failure naming the created issues, with `error_type=decomposition_application_failed`. New state fields are persisted to the resume record, so re-entry reuses the created-slice map and creates only what is missing — a fully applied split re-entered makes no gh call at all. Audit gained `preflight_complexity_gate.assessment_application` (record schema v46 → v47 with `_migrate_v46_to_v47`).

story_deviations: The spec does not say how a `decline` ends the run. Implemented as terminal 'returned for decomposition' with no mutation (the original stays open and runnable, satisfying the AC), on the reading that declining a split is not approving the scope. Flagging in case the intended behaviour was to continue the run.

`accept` is not offered for bug-typed originals or file-backed stories. A bug slice would need an observed/expected/diagnosis body this path has no evidence to write and would be refused by the shape gate; a file-backed story has no issue to close. Both are mechanical refusals to offer, not silent failures.
